summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute on chronic pancreatitis and persistent Herbaspirillum species bacteremia originating from her port-a-cath, which she was in the process of completing a ceftazidime course for at the time of presentation. Despite initial continuation of ceftazidime, blood cultures remained positive, prompting infectious disease consultation and a switch to Zosyn. The decision was made to remove the infected port-a-cath and place a temporary central venous line, which was successfully performed. The patient improved steadily with pain and nausea control, advancement to a regular diet, and resolution of bacteremia, with all subsequent blood cultures negative. Her anticoagulation was managed through fluctuations in INR, ultimately being bridged back to Coumadin with a Lovenox dose prior to discharge. Hypertension was controlled by increasing lisinopril, and antibiotic-associated diarrhea resolved. She was discharged home with home health services, oral ciprofloxacin to complete infection treatment, updated medication regimen, and follow-up plans including pain management and gastroenterology appointments.
